newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest spot power holds mostly steady to lower.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest spot power holds mostly steady to lower.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the midwestern U.S. were mostly steady Wednesday as normal temperatures through much of the region kept demand at moderate levels, industry sources said.
Temperatures through much of the Mid-West were expected to be near normal through the area most of the week.
Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP), Thursday peak, non-firm power prices were discussed steady at $17.00-19.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), the brokers and marketers said.
Off-peak Thursday non-firm MAPP power was reported to be steady at $11.00-13.00, the sources said.
In the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN), peak, non-firm power prices for Thursday were talked steady at $16.00-18.00, the sources said.
MAIN off peak next day power was also said to be unchanged at $11.00-12.00 per MWh.

Peak, non-firm electricity prices in the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR) for Thursday were reported to be steady to slightly lower at $14.50-16.50 from $15.00-17.00 on Tuesday, the sources said.
ECAR electricity prices for off-peak, non-firm delivery were notionally assessed steady at $13.00-15.00 per MWh.
February ECAR was said to have eased to $22.00-22.50 from $22.50-23.00 per MWh on Tuesday, while March ECAR peak power was said to be talked at $20.00-20.50 per MWh.

In the Southwest Power Pool (SPP) peak, non-firm power prices for Thursday delivery were talked at $14.00-16.00 in the south and steady at $16.00-18.00 in the north from $16.00-18.00 through the entire region on Tuesday.
Off-peak next day prices throughout SPP were pegged steady at $11.00-13.00 per MWh.
February SPP was said to be steady to lower at $22.00-23.00 from $22.50-23.00 per MWh on Tuesday, while March peak SPP was assessed at $20.50-20.85 per MWh.

Separately, PECO Energy Co trimmed power production at the 1,055 megawatt unit 2 at its Limerick nuclear generating station in Pottsdam, Pa., for repairs, a Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) spokesman said.
The PECO unit should ramp back up to near 75 percent of capacity by Thursday, then continue scaling down operations ahead of a 25-day refueling outage set to begin January 31.
